subject: computer-science
title: System Architecture: Fetch-Execute Cycle
welcome_lead: Watch the CPU work — fetch, decode, execute, repeat.
meta_desc: GCSE Computer Science adventure on the fetch-execute cycle and key CPU registers.
final_note: You can describe how the CPU runs every single instruction.

concepts.def: Get the next instruction from memory.
Work out what the instruction means.
Program counter — holds next instruction's address.
Memory address register — address being accessed.
Memory data register — data being transferred.

walkthroughs.body_html:
1. Fetch: PC points at next instruction; CU loads it via MAR/MDR
  2. Decode: CU works out which operation it is
  3. Execute: ALU (if maths) or CU performs it; PC advances

• PC: address of next instruction
  • MAR: address being read/written
  • MDR: data being read/written
  • ACC: accumulator — holds ALU results
Suppose PC = 12. Fetch: read RAM address 12 into MDR. Decode: it's ADD 5. Execute: ALU adds 5 to ACC; PC becomes 13. Ready for the next.
